segments.title: Chương 217: Thần tượng trẻ
segments.content:
Chapter 220: 0217 Youth Idol (Note: The part about the concerted action agreement has been revised. Old Wang doesn't know anything. My thanks to the experts for their corrections.)

While the negotiations were at a stalemate, YouTube's financing round in the US also concluded. A post-money valuation of 150 million USD!

Tudou.com's value rose accordingly.

ByteDance's financing negotiations also became much smoother.

"Mr. Chen, this is our final valuation," Yang Lin emphasized. "It's not that we underestimated ByteDance before, but rather because Tudou.com's prospects have been bullish recently."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Understood."

ByteDance's pre-money valuation was 230 million USD.

Carlyle Group led the round with 26 million USD. SoftBank followed with 8.5 million USD. DCM followed with 8 million USD. IDG added another 1.5 million USD. DFJ added another 2 million USD.

The total Series B financing amounted to 46 million USD. The post-money valuation was 276 million USD.

The equity structure was changed to:

Chen Guiliang 53.67%. Guo Feng 4.67%.

Carlyle 9.42%. SoftBank 3.08%. DCM 2.90%.

Option pool 11.11%.

In addition, Chen Guiliang's sole right to nominate independent directors could be held for now, but must be relinquished before the IPO. His veto power over the removal of independent directors was not supported by the investors.

Also, the investors rejected the provision regarding Chen Guiliang's veto power over amending the articles of association. His veto power over the appointment and removal of senior executives could be retained, but must be relinquished before the IPO.

Everything was for the sake of a successful IPO.

"A pleasure working with you."

"A pleasure working with you."

All parties reached a preliminary agreement, and the detailed due diligence process would follow.

The official signing was estimated to happen in about half a month.

The university sports meet had already begun.

There were proper Olympic events, as well as fun competitions like tug-of-war.

"Go! Go!"

Men and women selected from several classes of the Yuanpei Program formed the Yuanpei Program tug-of-war team. Their first opponent was the team from the College of Mechanics and Engineering.

Chen Guiliang strained with all his might and finally managed to stabilize their precarious position.

After a stalemate of a full three minutes, the Yuanpei team began to chant and counterattack, pulling their opponents over bit by bit.

"Mechanics, Mechanics, our strength never wanes! One, two, one, two, one, two..."

The guys and girls from the Mechanics department also started chanting and pulling in unison.

The cheerleaders from both sides crowded closer and closer, as if they wished they could jump in and pull the rope themselves.

Zhao Beibei was jumping up and down on the side, cheering on Chen Guiliang and his team: "Yuanpei, Yuanpei, who else but us! Yuanpei, Yuanpei..."

There were even some fangirls from a neighboring college who ran over to cheer for Chen Guiliang: "Chen Guiliang, you're the best!"

Chen Guiliang was really giving it his all, but his team's overall strength was not as good as their opponent's. During the continuous, rhythmic pulling, some members of the Yuanpei team had already lost their rhythm, unable to effectively pull together with the team.

Moreover, on the opposing Mechanics team, there were two burly, stout men standing at the back.

The Yuanpei team didn't have a single person of that build.

"Damn it!"

Chen Guiliang was still pulling, but he saw that several of his teammates in front of him had lost their balance. The rope in his hands was pulled away irresistibly, and Chen Guiliang was also thrown off balance.

After a stalemate that had lasted several minutes, the winner was decided in that single instant.

It was a total rout.

Several members of the Yuanpei team, physically exhausted, sat down on the ground.

There was also a female member of the Yuanpei team who felt she hadn't performed well and had dragged the whole team down, and she started wiping her tears and crying on the spot.

The victorious Mechanics students came over very friendly to shake hands.

Chen Guiliang's hands clenched and unclenched. His palms were burning. He took a moment to calm his breathing and smiled as he shook hands and exchanged words with the other team.

Damn, with the strength of the Mechanics department, they could probably make it to the semi-finals in the tug-of-war competition.

The Yuanpei team had bad luck, meeting a strong opponent in the very first round.

Chen Guiliang pulled up the two guys who were sitting on the ground, then went to comfort the crying girl.

"Chen Guiliang!"

Director Zhu was waving at him from the side of the field, with President Xu standing beside him.

Chen Guiliang walked over slowly with his hands on his hips. He had exhausted his strength just now and hadn't recovered yet.

"Hello, President Xu. Hello, Director Zhu."

Chen Guiliang greeted them.

President Xu smiled in approval. "Not bad, actively participating in school and department activities."

Chen Guiliang said, "It's a shame we lost in the first round."

"Victory and defeat are common in battle," President Xu commented. "The Yuanpei team members are generally of a weaker build. They don't have those big guys at the back like the Mechanics department. To be able to hold on for so long is already very good."

Chen Guiliang strolled along the edge of the sports field with the two university leaders.

After walking for a while, they stopped again. The short-distance race was about to begin.

"How are the Series B financing talks going?" President Xu asked, looking at the sprinters who were warming up.

Chen Guiliang said, "We should be able to sign by the end of this month."

President Xu praised, "You are Peking University's entrepreneurial role model. The university has decided to recommend you for the 'Beijing Youth Role Model' selection."

"Thank you for the recognition from the leadership." Chen Guiliang had never heard of this selection event.

The event was divided into three lists: Beijing's Ten Outstanding Youths, Outstanding Young Entrepreneurs (10 gold prize winners), and the Capital Contribution Award for Entrepreneurial Youth (10 gold prize winners).

The Ten Outstanding Youths was the most prestigious, and Chen Guiliang figured he probably wouldn't be selected.

The Capital Contribution Award for Entrepreneurial Youth would also depend on luck. The CEO of Shougang Group, the CEO of Beijing Urban Construction, the CEO of Tsinghua Unigroup, the director of the Beijing Cigarette Factory... these big shots were definitely on the list.

Chen Guiliang would most likely be selected as an Outstanding Young Entrepreneur.

"Bang!"

The starting pistol fired, and the sprinters shot out.

Chen Guiliang felt the surrounding cheers were like a tsunami.

"Go, go!"

Chen Guiliang also started shouting, because a third-year senior from the Yuanpei Program was currently running in third place.

"Yes! Beautiful!"

Just before reaching the finish line, that third-year senior overtook another runner, finishing second in his preliminary heat. This was a pleasant surprise.

After applauding the athletes, President Xu said, "There's an entrepreneurship lecture in May. Are you free to attend? Wang Zhidong, Lei Ming, Chen Hua, and Wu Minhui will also be there."

"I will definitely attend," Chen Guiliang immediately agreed.

These were all Peking University alumni.

Wang Zhidong was the founder of Sina, who had already been kicked out. He was currently working on the KGEN Collaborative Application Platform.

Lei Ming was the former CTO of Baidu and was now the founder of Kuwo Music.

Chen Hua was the founder of Kuxun. He had just received 2 million USD in venture capital and would receive another 10 million USD in half a year.

Although Kuxun had just been founded, its core team was full of future tycoons, having produced over 30 entrepreneurs. They were even jokingly called the "Kuxun Gang." For instance, the company's first engineer was named Zhang Yiming, the very same one from today's Toutiao and ByteDance.

Yes, at this moment, Zhang Yiming was working in the Peking University Science Park. He just needed to take the elevator upstairs to get to Chen Guiliang's ByteDance company...

Wu Minhui was in enterprise data services and would later transition to big data and artificial intelligence. Sequoia Capital was still negotiating with him, and he was expected to receive an investment of 8 to 10 million USD.

This year had already entered the era of frenzied investment, with a large number of startups receiving funding.

Within the Peking University Science Park alone, more than one or two companies had received venture capital. That was why Peking University was preparing to hold an entrepreneurship lecture, inviting alumni who had achieved success in their ventures to come back and participate.

At the end of April, ByteDance held the signing ceremony for its Series B financing.

This time, not only did the leaders of the Science Park Company and the Incubator Company attend, but President Xu from Peking University also came to make an appearance.

The venue for the ceremony was chosen in the Innovation Center building, which was completed at the end of last year.

Zhang Yiming came to work at the company early in the morning. Seeing the festive balloons and banners, he said to his colleague Xie Xin (the future Vice President of Toutiao), "It's so lively over there."

Xie Xin tucked a strand of hair behind her ear. "It's a huge financing round, so it certainly deserves to be grand. We only got 2 million USD in venture capital last month. It would have been quite impressive last year, but this year it's nothing to speak of."
